A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRAFT research, with matching authors, methods, and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original CRAFT safety and reasoning results, component ablations, and evaluations against GPTFuzzer and AutoDAN in Tables 1–3 and Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, additional latent-geometry experiments, and LlamaGuard evaluation in Tables 1–5 and the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The LCLR stage, its three losses, and the GRPO-based R2L stage with latent, textual, and consistency rewards remain unchanged. Clarified trace labeling and the added textual-reward ablation do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both retain R2D-R1 training data, JailbreakBench and StrongReject safety evaluation, AIME24, MATH-500, Minerva, and LiveCodeBench, alongside the same jailbreak attack coverage. The added geometry analyses and alternative evaluator do not introduce a new dataset, application domain, or task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain SafeChain, RealSafe, STAR, SafeKey, IPO, and ReasoningShield, plus the base models. The new LlamaGuard comparison uses the same comparator set. Updated publication years do not indicate changed baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds LlamaGuard evaluation on JailbreakBench and full-space and before/after geometry protocols, including Qwen3-0.6B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct configurations. Existing prompt counts, benchmark metrics, and decoding settings retain their reported values. Appendix G mentions extended training without specifying a revised training budget.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Table 3 adds removal of R_txt; Sections 6.4–6.5 test RETHINK geometry beyond PCA and examine representations before and after training; Appendix H adds model comparisons; Appendix F tests sensitivity to the safety evaluator. The existing GPTFuzzer/AutoDAN analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both state that experiments use three distinct random seeds and report mean and standard deviation. Tables 1–3 retain the statement that variances are omitted because they are at most 0.2%. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace CRAFT scores while retaining baseline values: DeepSeek/Qwen defense averages change from 0.074/0.117 to 0.062/0.099, and Pass@1 averages from 0.468/0.585 to 0.481/0.602. Table 3 changes the full-model average from 0.082 to 0.099 and adds the R_txt ablation at 0.279. Tables 4–5 and Figures 5/7 add geometry and evaluator-validation results. Figure 4 remains unchanged; the PDFs do not specify the training-budget difference underlying the replaced scores.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.1 becomes Proposition 5.1 with a substantively different guarantee: an error bound attributed to reward variance and policy entropy is replaced by C times the latent perturbation radius, with C depending on Lipschitz constants. Appendix C replaces the earlier proof with an expanded derivation. Section 6.4 also introduces formal centroid, safety-axis, and projection-coefficient definitions.

C1.justification: The main methodological contributions and claimed exclusion of superficial alignment remain. However, the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion strengthen the advertised quantitative benefits: reasoning safety rises from 79.0% to 82.1%, response safety from 87.7% to 89.6%, and reasoning-performance improvement from 4.7% to 8.0%.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of PCA displacement, RETHINK's position along the safety axis, and representation changes after training. Appendix F interprets alternative-evaluator results as evidence against metric-specific optimization. New Appendices B and G specify adversarial-prompting scope, computational costs, required training per model family, unestablished cross-family transfer, and lack of validation against fully adaptive attacks.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the anonymous code link and future-release promise with a named GitHub code link in the abstract. Section 3 newly documents R2D-R1 self-evaluation labels and LlamaGuard validation. Hardware, software libraries, temperature, top-p, and token-limit disclosures remain unchanged; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V2 condenses the general reasoning survey, removing references such as Tree-of-Thoughts, Graph-of-Thoughts, and self-refinement work. It adds citations including TIDES, autonomous jailbreak agents, adversarial reasoning, Llama Guard, and GenoArmory. Positioning against the principal reasoning defenses remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most method and experimental prose and the main section sequence are retained. The LLM-alignment discussion moves into the main related-work section, the shortened LRM survey moves to Appendix A, and references move before the appendices. V2 also corrects wording and expands acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, replaces the separate cover and main contents arrangement, and extensively redistributes retained displays. It adds Tables 4–5 and Figures 5 and 7, expands Table 3, and reformats the retained evaluation-prompt figure from Figure 5 to Figure 6.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful checks absent from v1: the R_txt ablation, alternative-evaluator validation, and quantitative geometry analyses. Explicit limitations improve transparency, and the full-model rows in Tables 1 and 3 now agree. These gains remain limited by unresolved reasoning in Appendix C: continuity does not establish that consistency-reward gains outweigh possible R_ls losses. Appendix F also overstates Table 5, where CRAFT's DeepSeek response score of 0.004 is worse than RealSafe and SafeKey at 0.003.
